create.name: Wild Flower Zen Sangha
create.bio:
Wild Flower Zen Sangha is a lay Zen community based in Paris, with affiliated groups in Portugal and practitioners who join online from elsewhere. It was founded by Roshi Amy Hollowell, an American-born Zen teacher and poet who has lived in France since 1981, after she received dharma transmission in 2004 from Roshi Catherine Genno Pagès of the Dana Sangha near Paris. Sensei Joa Scetbon, her successor, also teaches for the sangha, leading a weekly evening sit in Paris and retreats of his own.

The community deliberately does without monks, priests, robes and a building of its own; its idea is that practice happens wherever life happens, and its name comes from the way wild flowers belong to their own place while growing everywhere. Each week there are early-morning sits on Zoom, a Thursday evening session with meditation and a dharma talk, a Saturday study group, and in-person sitting in Paris, Arles and the Drôme. Through the year it runs days of practice in Paris and residential retreats in France and Portugal, including 'retreats in the heart of life' held in everyday surroundings. The sangha is a French non-profit association; activities are offered for suggested donations.

courses.title: Retreats and Day Practice
courses.description: The sangha's retreat programme, mostly led by Roshi Amy Hollowell with some by Sensei Joa Scetbon: days of practice in Paris that can also be joined online, and weekend and week-long residential retreats in France and Portugal. Participants become members of the association.

free_resources.title: WFZ-Méditations
free_resources.description: How to join the sangha's regular sitting: weekday early-morning meditation and a Thursday evening dharma session on Zoom (Paris time), plus in-person groups in Paris, Arles and the Drôme. Online practice is by donation; email for the Zoom link.
